steps.prompt: Start with $1, 1$. Each new number is the sum of the two before it. Write the first ten numbers. What do you notice about every third one?

cards.title: Each term from the ones before
cards.body: A recursive rule like $a_{n + 1} = 2a_n + 1$ builds each term from earlier terms, starting from given values. Work out the first few terms carefully. Often a pattern appears that you can then prove or trust.

steps.text: Each term is one less than a power of $2$: $a_n = 2^n - 1$. So $a_{10} = 1024 - 1 = 1023$.

cards.title: Counting with recursion
cards.body: To count the ways to climb $n$ stairs taking $1$ or $2$ steps at a time, look at the LAST step: it was a $1$ (from stair $n - 1$) or a $2$ (from stair $n - 2$). So $W(n) = W(n - 1) + W(n - 2)$, with $W(1) = 1$ and $W(2) = 2$.

cards.title: Worked example: climbing stairs
cards.problem: In how many ways can you climb $6$ stairs taking $1$ or $2$ steps at a time?

cards.title: The common trap: off by one
cards.body: Check whether the sequence starts at $a_0$ or $a_1$, and count terms carefully: $a_5$ is the FIFTH term when you start at $a_1$. Use the starting values given. And test a pattern on at least four terms before trusting it.

prompts: Explain why the number of ways to climb $n$ stairs is $W(n - 1) + W(n - 2)$.
